ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a nitrogen-containing five-membered saturated ring, and the nitrogen is labeled with a positive charge. The nitrogen is connected to the upper chiral carbon, which bears a dashed-wedge H and is connected to the carbon center on the right. The right carbon center is connected to O and bears two Ph substituents, one represented with a solid wedge and one with a dashed wedge. O is further connected to B below; B is also connected to R, and forms a B/O/N-containing ring with the positively charged nitrogen. There is also a negatively charged BH3/BH4-type borohydride part at the bottom of the figure, and the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: According to the specified transcription method, start with R as a wildcard substituent connected to boron and write it as *B1; proceed along the ring through O to the tertiary carbon connected to two phenyl groups, giving *B1OC(c2ccccc2)(c2ccccc2); continue to the chiral CH in the figure, written as [C@@H]2 according to the shown wedge/dashed configuration; then proceed along the saturated carbon chain CCC back to the positively charged nitrogen, and use [NH+]12 to close simultaneously to boron and the chiral carbon; finally write the lower negatively charged borohydride as a disconnected counterion .[BH4-]. Therefore the overall SMILES is *B1OC(c2ccccc2)(c2ccccc2)[C@@H]2CCC[NH+]12.[BH4-].

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: Transcribe the molecular graph directly from the image into SMILES. Start at the variable R substituent as wildcard attached to boron: *B1. Follow the ring through O to the tertiary carbon bearing two phenyl branches: *B1OC(c2ccccc2)(c2ccccc2). Continue to the stereogenic CH in the proline ring, assigning the configuration from the wedge/dash bonds as [C@@H]2. Complete the saturated carbon chain CCC back to the positively charged nitrogen, and close the nitrogen to both boron and the chiral carbon using [NH+]12. Finally add the disconnected borohydride counterion read from the BH3/negative portion as .[BH4-]. The resulting SMILES is *B1OC(c2ccccc2)(c2ccccc2)[C@@H]2CCC[NH+]12.[BH4-].
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中左侧是一个含氮五元饱和环，氮标为正电荷。氮与上方手性碳相连，该手性碳带有一个虚线楔形的 H，并连接到右侧的碳中心。右侧碳中心连有 O，并带两个 Ph 取代基，其中一个用实楔、一个用虚楔表示。O 再连到下方的 B，B 还连有 R，并与带正电的氮构成含 B/O/N 的环。图中下方还有带负电的 BH3/BH4 型硼氢部分，题目要求忽略箭头。推理：按指定转写方法，从 R 作为通配取代基连接到硼开始写为 *B1；沿环经过 O 到连两个苯基的叔碳，得到 *B1OC(c2ccccc2)(c2ccccc2)；继续到图中手性 CH，按所示楔/虚线构型写作 [C@@H]2；再沿饱和碳链 CCC 回到带正电的氮，并用 [NH+]12 同时闭合到硼和手性碳；最后把下方负电硼氢作为断开的抗衡离子写为 .[BH4-]。因此整体 SMILES 为 *B1OC(c2ccccc2)(c2ccccc2)[C@@H]2CCC[NH+]12.[BH4-]。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct structure-to-SMILES transcription is the only genuinely needed route: identify the molecular graph, charges, stereocenter, substituents, and disconnected borohydride fragment from the drawing, then encode them in SMILES.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the drawn structure: a boron-containing ring with B bonded to R, O, and the positively charged proline-like nitrogen; O bonded to a tertiary carbon bearing two Ph groups; that carbon bonded to a chiral CH shown with wedge/dash H; the chiral carbon is part of a five-membered saturated N-heterocycle ending at [NH+]. Also read the separate N-to-BH3 arrow/borohydride depiction as the counterion fragment to be represented as [BH4-], while ignoring the arrow itself as instructed.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question instruction that the target is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure and that arrows should be ignored, so arrowheads are not encoded as bonds or reaction notation.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply skeletal-structure-to-SMILES rules: encode R as wildcard *, each phenyl as c2ccccc2, use ring-closure digits to represent the fused B/O/C/N/proline ring system, bracket charged nitrogen as [NH+], encode the anionic borohydride as a separate disconnected component [BH4-], and use the wedge/dash stereochemistry at the CH center to choose [C@@H].
